waivers.reason: Reviewed security fixes #387, #388, and #391 touch existing platform/configuration and editor-view debt; some existing lookups and Win32 handles are reclassified when their enclosing lines change, and native lifetime tests exercise Win32 handles. Preserve the exact raw findings and reject later file changes until the debt or matching is addressed in #389.

The CI dependency-age fix in #390 touches an existing build workflow. Its two focused Rust integration filters are intentional additional tests with explicit executed-count checks; removing either would weaken coverage. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject further unreviewed workflow changes.

The #395 settings-watch rebuild-loop fix touches existing configuration-watch debt: the noexcept containment catch-alls, the plain request value struct, and stop/fake-state findings in the two watch test files. The fix adds no new findings; reducing that unrelated debt would widen a crash fix. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

The #398 terminal menu/focus/Run Task fixes, the #401 Split Down button, and #402 Phase A agent presence (job-membership hints, the window-owned tracker, and the Projects agent rows, including OpenCode and Pi) touch existing terminal session/window, editor-window, and Projects debt. Each new finding was reviewed: catch-alls are noexcept containment at callback, worker, and join boundaries; public fields are plain event, option, and record value structs or members of pimpl-internal state and of the presence tracker's private per-tab state; HWND mentions are the Projects page's own window and native test fixtures; the job-notification std::thread is always joined by Close, which the destructor calls; the mutable member is a test fake's counter; and the private-include matches are the regex hit on terminal/window headers already included beside them. Reducing unrelated debt would widen these changes. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

The #402 Phase A follow-up re-touches files reviewed for 88ec66d76: Projects agent rows now show only the agent name (Herdr's default), and the agent's glyph-stripped terminal session title becomes the row's hover text, reported by the presence tracker when it changes for a present agent. Each new finding was reviewed: the sessionTitle and tooltip members are fields of plain record value structs (TerminalAgentPresenceRecord, ProjectAgentEntry, ProjectsRow) and of the presence tracker's private per-tab state; the Win32 mentions are the Projects page's own tooltip and LISTBOX messages and native test fixtures (a hidden parent window, the tooltip lookup, and its test-local search struct). The remaining findings and missing reductions are the previous record's debt with shifted lines. Reducing unrelated debt would widen this change. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

#403 tmux panel reconciliation re-touches files reviewed for 88ec66d76 and 5964b0a16 and the tmux facade: tmux commands now resolve their implicit target from the authenticated caller pane, the topology model honors -d, the runtime announces topology changes, and the panel adopts, removes and selects terminals to match. Each new finding was reviewed: TmuxCallerContext::paneId and the TerminalTabAdoption / TerminalTabTopologyReconcileResult members are fields of plain value structs; the TmuxCli.h and TmuxCommandDispatcher.h hits are a defaulted function parameter that the scanner reads as a field; lastRuntimeCurrentPane is pimpl-internal state; the two catch-alls in TerminalTabManager.cpp are the advisory event-publish boundary (as in PublishTabEvent) and reconcile containment that returns the consistent partial result; the HWND mentions are the panel's own pane windows (PaneHasKeyboardFocus) and native test fixtures; the runtime test's Subscribe result is an RAII TerminalSubscription released before the service. The remaining findings and missing reductions are the previous records' debt with shifted lines. Reducing unrelated debt would widen this change. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

#404 moves the title-bar Update indicator to the front of the title-control run, as VS Code did in 84ed7dda5 (#330726): CalculateCustomFrameLayout emits it before the Layout control, and kTitleControls and the CCustomTitleBar::Paint loop list it first so hit testing, painting and UIA order follow. No new finding is added; the touched files keep their pre-existing ratchet debt, and reducing unrelated debt would widen a placement fix. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

#407 gives the Projects list the shared VS Code overlay scrollbar (a new ListBoxOverlayScrolling helper that the Projects page and the Source Control lists both use for the explicit list-box scroll model and wheel scrolling), #409 indents Projects child rows by Explorer's 12 DIP per level, and #410 makes Codex and Devin sessions appear: AgentSessionHistory's JSON parser accepts the trailing whitespace Devin's CLI prints, and the Projects page reruns discovery on a bounded back-off (at most 12 attempts, 5 s doubling to 60 s) while an agent has no session of its own yet. Each new finding was reviewed: the public fields are members of the plain ProjectAgentSighting value struct and of test fixtures; the catch-alls are noexcept containment around the overlay scrollbar's creation and update, which fail closed to the list without an overlay; the SetTimer acquisition is released by StopSessionCatchUp on every tick, deactivation and Cleanup; the HWND mentions are the list box the helpers read and native test fixtures. The remaining findings and missing reductions are the previous records' debt with shifted lines. Reducing unrelated debt would widen this change. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

#411 splits the Projects ViewContainer into two Views, Projects and Sessions, the way Explorer holds Explorer and Outline: the manifest declares sakura.agentSessions beside sakura.projects, CEditWnd's provider switches to factoryForContainer so one page renders both, ProjectsModel gains the ProjectAgentSessions projection, and a new CProjectsListPane owns one View's list mechanics (owner-drawn list box, the #407 overlay scrollbar, its tooltip tool, the #412 single-click gesture and the empty message) that the page's two panes share; the page paints VS Code's pane headers, collapses a View on a header click and moves the boundary with a 4 DIP sash. These files also carry the reviewed #407/#409/#410 changes of the previous record. Each new finding was reviewed: the public fields are members of the plain AgentSessionsRow, AgentSessionsProjection, ProjectsTexts and ProjectsListPaneCallbacks value types and of test fixtures; the catch-alls are noexcept containment around std::function callbacks and string allocation, each failing closed to no rows, no tooltip text or no action; the HWND/WPARAM/LPARAM mentions are the pane's own list box, its tooltip tool and native test fixtures. The remaining findings and missing reductions are the previous records' debt with shifted lines. Reducing unrelated debt would widen this change. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

#408 adds the Sessions view's context menu (resume, rename, pin, archive, delete, copy, display count): AgentSessionManagement is the pure menu and view-state model, AgentSessionStoreOperations renames and deletes a session in the agent's own store, AgentSessionViewStateService persists pins, archive marks and the display count through the existing Project catalog store adapter under its own key, discovery reads marked sessions first, BoundedProcessRunner can hold standard input open until a borrowed event, and CProjectsPage, CEditWnd and the runtime compose them. These files also carry the reviewed #407/#409/#410/#411/#412 changes of the previous record. Each new finding was reviewed: the public fields are members of plain value types (AgentSessionViewState, AgentSessionMenuItem, AgentSessionStoreContext and its tools and services, ProjectAgentSessionsQuery, ProjectAgentSessionManagement, AgentSessionsRow, discovery limits) and of test fixtures; the catch-alls are noexcept containment around std::function seams, allocation and the two store-operation entry points, each failing closed to Failed, no menu or no action; the stop event of the single-flight rename/delete worker is closed by ReleaseSessionOperation after the worker is joined on every path including Cleanup; the HWND/WPARAM/LPARAM mentions are the page's own list box, its popup menu and native test fixtures. The remaining findings and missing reductions are the previous records' debt with shifted lines. Reducing unrelated debt would widen this change. Track the pre-existing ratchet debt in #389 and reject later unreviewed changes to these files.

#406 Phase 2 restores agent sessions when a Project is opened: AgentSessionRestore is the pure record, codec and per-open plan model (plain value-struct fields), AgentSessionRestoreService persists it under its own key, and CEditWnd_AgentSessionRestore wires record-on-close and one bounded restore attempt into the window. Its catch-alls are noexcept containment with defined fallbacks (record nothing, restore nothing), and the restore SetTimer and stop event are released by CancelAgentSessionRestore and PollAgentSessionRestore on every path. The test includes the model's own header.

#413 cuts New Window latency: SenpManagementService overlaps its read-only sakura-senp-tool runs on the window startup path and splits the installed listing into ReadInstalledListings / AdoptInstalledListings, SenpLanguageService loads grammars concurrently and adopts them in declaration order, and CWorkbenchRuntime::Start plus StartupTrace gain four named trace events. Each item was reviewed: the two new public fields are the members of InstalledListings, a plain value struct that is a private nested type of CWin32SenpManagementService and carries the two tool results between the read and the adoption; the four touched files keep their baseline findings because the change adds trace marks, includes and concurrency around existing calls and removes none of the reviewed constructs, so no reduction was available without unrelated refactoring.

#413 creates a view pane's title action buttons and their shared tooltip on first use instead of for every pane at window start. Each item was reviewed: the boundary.win32_type finding in SenpViewContainer.cpp is the TTM_ADDTOOLW SendMessageW/LPARAM call that already existed in Initialize and only moved into the new EnsureActionControl helper inside the same native view container implementation, which is the Win32 owner of these HWNDs; no Win32 type crosses a new boundary. SenpViewContainerTest.cpp gains one native-window test (TitleActionButtonsExistFromTheirFirstUseAndKeepTheirOrder) and its 15 baseline findings are the fixture's existing Win32 usage, which this change does not touch and cannot reduce without rewriting an unrelated fixture.

#413 caches the built-in catalog and the installed listings beside the install root: SenpManagementService.h declares the pure EncodeBuiltInCatalogCache / DecodeBuiltInCatalogCache and EncodeInstalledListingsCache / DecodeInstalledListingsCache record codecs and InstalledStoreStamp next to the existing detail seam, and SenpBuiltInStartupTest.cpp gains tests of those codecs and of the stamp. Each item was reviewed: the two state.public_mutable_field findings are the installed / uninstalled members of InstalledListings, the private nested value struct of CWin32SenpManagementService that carries the two raw tool results from ReadInstalledListings to AdoptInstalledListings and is never shared state; they only moved down with the added declarations. The header's 64 and the test's 7 baseline findings are existing declarations and fixtures this change does not touch and cannot reduce without an unrelated rewrite.
